note: Grouped the raw table on the exact proposed key (year, state_fips, district, stage, candidate_name, party, vote_mode): 81 groups still have >1 row; two are genuine same-candidate collisions ('Lee Fletcher'/'Rodney Alexander', LA-05, 2002) caused by Louisiana's jungle-primary runoff being coded under the same stage='gen', distinguished only by the RUNOFF flag — a column the mart already selects as is_runoff but left out of the key (the same missing-coverage-period mistake flagged in CLAUDE.md); adding it does resolve those two but 79 residual groups are unresolvable 'NA'-placeholder-candidate rows with no disambiguating column available at all.

Grouped the raw table on the proposed key (year, state_fips, candidate_name, party): 6 real duplicate groups exist, and inspecting them shows each pair is the same candidate's regular-ballot tally vs. write-in tally (e.g. Clinton/Trump, Maryland 2016) distinguished by the WRITEIN flag, which the mart already selects as is_writein but omits from the key; adding is_writein to the key was verified to make it perfectly unique (3740 groups = 3740 rows, 0 dups).

Grouped the raw table on the proposed key (year, state_fips, stage, candidate_name, party_detailed, vote_mode): 62 duplicate groups exist; a verified real case (Alex Padilla, California 2022, regular vs. special election, same year/stage/party/mode) is only distinguished by the SPECIAL flag, which the mart selects as is_special_election but leaves out of the key — the same available-but-unused-disambiguator mistake as the house mart; remaining dups are mostly blank-candidate sentinel rows plus at least one Louisiana general/runoff pair this source has no flag column to distinguish at all.

Confirmed try_to_number(country_territory) is NULL for all 2723 rows as claimed, but the raw (untransformed) COUNTRY_TERRITORY text column combined with EDITION gives exactly 2723 distinct combos for 2723 rows — a perfect key was sitting right there; the skip reasoning correctly spotted the cast bug but wrongly concluded no usable identifier existed instead of flagging the cast as the thing to fix.

The mart is an unfiltered passthrough of FED_ICE_STATISTICS with no dedup, and a live query on the exact claimed 9-column key shows only 203 distinct combos across 221 rows -- 18 rows with metric_type='unknown' and every other column blank collide as exact duplicates, plus 2 more with metric_type='removals', so the 'clean OLAP-style fact table' claim is false and this test will fail against real data.

The mart is an unfiltered passthrough of FED_USCIS_DATA, and a live query on the exact claimed 10-column key shows only 154 distinct combos across 3,204 rows -- e.g. 561 rows share form_number/category/country/uscis_office all blank with the same report_title/source_file_url (parser junk/footnote rows, not per-form breakdowns), so the claimed 'one row per form/fiscal-period/category/country/office breakdown' grain does not hold and this test will fail massively against real data.

The chosen key uses REFUGEES_BY_COUNTRY_OF_ORIGIN -- the metric/count column -- instead of ENTITY as the identity dimension; live query confirms (entity, year, code) is already fully unique across all 7,442 rows (as good a key as the chosen one, with zero collisions either way today), so using a measure column as part of the uniqueness key is fragile and semantically wrong even though it happens not to misfire on the current snapshot -- the staging model's own header comment for this appears to be a generator bug (line 3 says grain is 'COUNTRY+YEAR+CODE' but line 4's natural_key hint substring-matched on '...COUNTRY...' in REFUGEES_BY_COUNTRY_OF_ORIGIN instead of ENTITY), which the agent copied verbatim without catching it against the real ENTITY column sitting right there in the same source.

This is exactly the masked-ID trap CLAUDE.md warns about: live query on FED_COURTLISTENER_FINANCIAL_DISCLOSURES shows only 66,286 distinct ID values across 108,770 rows, and the duplicate ID values sampled are garbage text fragments -- '|' (1,997x), 'i' (898x), '?' (813x), '-' (729x), 'Part VII' (685x), 'a', 'Value', '=' -- not a real CourtListener API primary key at all, so 'ID is CourtListener's own API primary key ... selected directly and unmodified' is factually false and this unique test will fail immediately.

Empirically disproven: (activity_id, case_number, registry_id) still leaves 16935 duplicate groups covering tens of thousands of rows out of 204019, and inspecting one group shows registry_id is a SITE-level FRS id (e.g. "FT WAINWRIGHT") under which many genuinely distinct buildings sit, each with its own facility_name/location_address (BLDG 3011, BLDG 3490, BLDG 5009 etc.) -- adding registry_id did not fix the collapse the agent claimed it fixed, and only the full 10-column select (adding facility_name/location_address) reaches the true 1-row-per-building grain (204019 distinct = total).

Empirically disproven: the chosen 5-column key leaves 3 duplicate groups that are legitimate distinct records -- e.g. the same activity_id/comp_monitor_uid/dates reported once under PGM_SYS_ACRNM='NEI' and once under 'NET', and another under 'RCRAINFO' vs 'CERCLIS' -- and adding PGM_SYS_ACRNM (already selected in the SQL, but omitted from the key) resolves all 3 to 0 duplicates, so as written the test will false-fail on real cross-program-system data, the same false-fail-on-legit-repeats mistake CLAUDE.md flags.

Empirically disproven and root-caused: ACCT_CODE is a 100%-blank sentinel column across all 121713 rows (COUNT(DISTINCT ACCT_CODE)=1, the exact masked-column trap CLAUDE.md warns about), so the real key is only (cu_number, cycle_date, table_name), which produces 7370 duplicate groups covering ~40k rows of clearly legitimate distinct records (e.g. 263 different physical branches of Navy Federal Credit Union under table_name='Credit Union Branch Information', each with a different branch name) that the source table has no other column to distinguish -- this needed either a skip (like fed_fec_committees) or a mixed-grain redesign, not a straight add.
